bull.b: Strong operating and free cash flow indicate high earnings-to-cash conversion, supporting internal funding, balance-sheet resilience and the company’s ability to invest through credit cycles.

Lower card delinquency and charge-off rates reduce expected credit costs and improve earnings visibility. Sustained improvement would support capital formation and profitability across the lending portfolio.

Progress on technology conversion and synergy realization can structurally improve scale, revenue opportunities and efficiency. Completing the integration should strengthen the combined payments and banking platform.

bear.b: Lower margins and volatile revenue weaken earnings consistency and reduce the cushion available to absorb credit losses, funding-cost changes or integration expenses over the medium term.

Capital and cash reductions constrain financial flexibility, particularly while risk-weighted assets, acquisitions and loan funding needs increase. Further buybacks or balance-sheet expansion could heighten this pressure.

bear.t: Integration Cost and Loan Growth Headwinds
bear.b: Elevated technology, marketing and integration spending can delay efficiency gains, while temporary Discover loan contraction limits near-term asset growth. The combined effects may moderate operating leverage until integration is complete.
